Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱer-der.?
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂der.?
Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂-der.?
Classical Persian زُرْنَا (zurnā)
Proto-Indo-European *ped-
Proto-Indo-European *-s
Proto-Indo-European *pṓds
Proto-Indo-Iranian *pā́ts
Proto-Iranian *pā́dah
Old Persian 𐎱𐎠𐎭 (p-a-d)
Classical Persian پَا (pā)
Classical Persian زُرْنَاپَا (zurnāpā)bor.
Classical Syriac ܙܪܝܦܐ (zārīp̄ā)bor.
Arabic زُرَافَة (zurāfa)bor.
Italian giraffabor.
Middle French giraffe
French girafe

    Inherited from Middle French giraffe, from Italian giraffa, from Arabic زُرَافَة (zurāfa).

    Noun

    [edit]

    girafe f (plural girafes)

    1. giraffe (mammal)
      une girafe mâle ― a male giraffe
    2. boom (a movable pole used to support a microphone or camera)
      (Can we add an example for this sense?)

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • girafeau m
    • girafon m

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • → Bulgarian: жираф (žiraf), жирафа (žirafa)
    • → Catalan: girafa
    • → Luxembourgish: Giraff
    • → Polish: żyrafa
      • → Kashubian: żirafa
    • → Romanian: girafă
    • → Russian: жираф (žiraf), жира́фа (žiráfa) — dated, colloquial, жира́фъ (žiráf) — pre-1918 spelling
      • → Georgian: ჟირაფი (žirapi)
      • → Ingrian: žirafa
    • → Swedish: giraff
      • → Finnish: kirahvi
